newsitem.title: JAPAN: France budget deficit to be 3% of GDP in 97 - Chirac.
newsitem.headline: France budget deficit to be 3% of GDP in 97 - Chirac.

text.p: France's fiscal budget deficit will be at three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) next year, French President Jacques Chirac told Japanese business executives in Tokyo on Tuesday.

"In two years, and despite difficult economic conditions, we have managed to reduce our public deficit from six percent to four percent of GDP and we will be at three percent next year," Chirac said in prepared speech that he will later deliver to the Keidanren business organisation.
"And this programme, I intend to pursue it," he said about France's budget deficit-cutting programme.
"For too long in Europe, public deficits have discouraged initiative and pulled down the economy. It was time to break the vicious cycle," he said.
On European monetary union, Chirac said: "Yes, Germany and France will be there at the Euro's rendez-vous."
"I am confident that we will succeed in this ambitious project which Chancellor Kohl, like myself, is strongly committed to," he added.
On financial systems, he said there remained a need to cooperate.

"If the development of trade is a powerful motor of growth, it is also one that holds new risks for the stability of the international monetary and financial system," he said. "That is why France believes it is greatly important that we re-enforce our cooperation to ensure the stability of the financial system."
"We must monitor the stability of our international financial system and prevent any dislocations," he added.
